newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $12.71 billion.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela foreign reserves rise to $12.71 billion.

text.p: Venezuela's foreign reserves rose $133 million, or 1.1 percent, to $12.711 billion in the week to Sept 30, according to figures released by the central bank Friday.

Reserves were up from $12.578 bln on Sept 24, the bank's latest weekly bulletin of indicators showed. Reserves are now up up $3.009 billion from levels of $9.702 billion on April 19 -- the last working day before exchange levels were lifted on April 22.
From the start of the year, reserve levels were up $2.988 billion, or 31 percent.

Venezuela's strengthening reserves position led Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar to announce this week that Venezuela would decline a second $500 million tranche of a $1.4 billion stand-by loan from the Intentional Monetary Fund.
Government officials had targeted foreign reserves to grow by $1.5 billion over the course of 1996 as part of Venezuela's IMF- supported economic adjustment program.
Venezuela's foreign reserves fell $1.784 billion, or 15.5 percent, in 1995 to end the year at $9.723 billion.
